title: Regeneration as descent to a free-energy attractor; induced shapes as local minima

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Regeneration as descent to a free-energy attractor; induced shapes as local minima

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: On the authors' proposed view, discrete planarian head patterns are the lowest free-energy outcomes of bioelectric network dynamics; amputation raises free energy and regeneration is a return to a low-energy attractor, octanol shifts the system to another attractor, and the induced other-species shapes are only local minima since worms return to the global minimum of G. dorotocephala morphology after about 3–4 weeks.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 3. Discussion › 3.7. A hypothesis: Physiological Network Attractors Underlie Regions of Anatomical Morphospace

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: On this view (Figure 9), the discrete head patterns are outcomes of bioelectric network dynamics with the lowest free-energy; cutting the network raises the free energy by deviating the system from its optimal morphology (damage), and initiates the regenerative process—a journey back down to a low-energy attractor.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M, Durant F, Hammelman J, Bessonov N, Volpert V, Morokuma J, Pinet K, Adams DS, Pietak A, Lobo D, Levin M, “Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms”, International journal of molecular sciences (2015), doi:10.3390/ijms161126065; section “3. Discussion › 3.7. A hypothesis: Physiological Network Attractors Underlie Regions of Anatomical Morphospace”. Scope: Planarian regeneration conceived as dynamics of a bioelectric network

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-girardia-20: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.14

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Calling regenerated forms minima and regeneration descent does not add a distinct observable prediction without a specified energy function. The same trajectories can always be redescribed post hoc as descent on a constructed landscape.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: A resolvable version would require an independently defined quantitative free-energy function over measured bioelectric and anatomical states whose gradients predict regeneration trajectories; the paper does not define such a function.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Free energy is used as an analogy without a fitted state function.

Observed return to morphology is compatible with many non-energy-based controllers.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.1
operationalizability: 0.25
discriminating power: 0.15
data adequacy: 0.05
analysis feasibility: 0.2

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The energetic wording redescribes amputation, regeneration, and later return to the species head. Morphology is both the phenomenon and the stand-in for free energy, so a non-energetic account of the same remodeling predicts the same observations. Existing shape records cannot separate the two.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Return from an induced head to Girardia shape over three to four weeks is a shape trajectory. Calling the induced shapes local free-energy minima and the species shape the global minimum restates that trajectory unless an energy is defined independently of the shape score.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No free-energy observable is defined apart from morphological closeness to the species target.

Any temporary deviant shape that later normalizes fits the local-minimum story.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.12
operationalizability: 0.3
data adequacy: 0.08
analysis feasibility: 0.2
discriminating power: 0.12
